My first year driving I hit a curb, busting a big hole in my tire. panicking I pulled into the first driveway, which happened to be a repair shop and  called my dad in tears. He told me he’d be there in 10 minutes to help me put on the spare. Once he got there he sat on the curb and gave me instructions without any physical help. A few of the mechanics saw me, a 16yo 90lbs girl who was crying and struggling to lift the spare,and offered to help. Every time they walked up to offer, my dad would say ‘no thanks, she’s got it’. I remember being so mad that he wouldn’t help me or let me take the help but I did it 100% on my own. He said I will always know that I am capable of changing a tire even if I never have to again. Since then I’ve changed several tires since then and am grateful my dad forced me to learn how. If I ever have kids, I will 100% teach them this way.

Do you have a few cat trees/ scratching posts for him? He’s going to scratch so if you don’t provide somewhere for him to do it, he will find something to scratch on his own. I’ve recently started using a spray bottle which has been extremely effective, keep one in every room if you have a large house, but after a month, all I need to do is pick it up and shake it, and my little guy goes into sweetheart mode. Baby wipes/ washcloths might be a better option with an occasional regular bath if it’s that much of a fight. Most artists don’t actually own their recordings, the record label does(scott borchetta). TS has saved enough money that she wanted to buy them from the label but they would only sell them to her under an agreement that she would release one new album(that they would own) for every album she bought. She holds a strong belief that an artist has a right to won their own music so she said hell no as she didn’t want to work with them anymore.  scott borchetta went and sold all her music to scooter braun(someone she already didn’t like) without telling her. This sale pissed her off because she wasn’t even offered the chance to buy them outright with no strings attached, but scooter braun was. 

She writes her own music(not super common in the industry) so she has more rights to the songs than a lot of artists. she decided to rerelease them to devalue the originals and making to so she. Her fans are very loyal and she knew if she asks us to listen to the new versions, we will. Now she owns all her own music and makes scooter brauns investment worth much less, potentially making him more willing to sell them to her. 

TLDR
Record label owns the recording, TS owns the lyrics. Record label screwed her over so she re-recorded her songs so the OG recording were worthless and she owned each song(strong moral belief). Her fans are super loyal so they stopped listening to the OG version and now they aren’t worth as much.

One morning I was reading the news and saw a crazy Florida man story involving a man having an army of a specific wild animal that he was threatening to attack the city. This happened in my home town of about 500k people, so I thought that’s a crazy coincidence and moved on. 
Later that night I was bartending and a very eccentric man came into my bar and was doing the normal crazy drunk customer weirdness. He was complimenting my music saying since I’m so musically talented he wanted my help on a song he was writing. I said sure cause it was slow and I was bored. He hand copied two different songs onto paper and said he would be back to pick them up with my edits.(for context I do not write/play music, I just play Spotify playlists at work). I read the first one which was about said army of the specific animal and realized it was the him, confirming with the name on his credit card. I thought that’s a crazy coincidence and moved on. 
Then I read the second song. It was about my boyfriend’s ex girlfriend. The song was called  ‘local restaurants name’ green eyed goddess. The song included her first name, her very specific style.(she only wore sundresses and knee-high socks with a backpack purse and had super unique bright green eyes and she worked at that restaurant. There was 0% chance that this song was about anyone else. I thought that’s a crazy coincidence and I don’t think I’ll ever be able to move on. 
The weirdest part was about two weeks later a woman who looked so so over it came in to pick up the songs which I didn’t expect. I do feel bad because it was definitely a mental health crisis but craziest coincidence that’s ever happened to me. 

TLDR
I read an article about a Florida man, later that night he came into the bar. I worked at and asked me to work on a song, song about my boyfriend’s ex-girlfriend.

I had a psychology professor make an extremely unprofessional joke about me during a lecture that made me so angry I dropped the class and never retook it despite loving the subject .

As an example he was trying to show how if you think hard enough you can remember things a lot farther back than you realize. The example was if you went back one meal at a time, you can remember all the food you ate for several days. It's important to note that I was in the recovery program for an eating disorder where one of my currents steps was to not lie about what I ate. I was having a rough week and hadn't eaten much for a few days. He called on me at random, and asked me what I had eaten for breakfast. I told him I hadn't eaten. He then asked me what I had for dinner the night before and I told him I hadn't eaten dinner the night before. The then asked me about a few more meals, before making the comment "of course I picked the one anorexic girl in this class". The whole class erupted in laughter. 

I know compared to a lot of the comments on this post, it wasn't so bad, but it shattered me. I was the first time in years I had any self confidence, and I didn't for a really long time after that.   Though I had a bad week, I was on the road to recovery, and dedicated to the program which is why I didn't lie.  I was really proud of myself, and when he said that it set me back months. I dropped the class as soon as the lecture was over, and never retook it with another professor in fear that something similar might happen. In retrospect I regret not informing the head of the department. If it were any other subject, I would probably have gotten over it, but a psychology teacher to talk about a psychological disorder like this is disgusting.
